requirements.behavior: Claim, defend, retry, cannot-claim, and ISO claim-response failures are surfaced.
Heartbeat cadence, disabling, retiming, and sequence rollover remain deterministic.
Addressed and broadcast ISO requests receive the required response or acknowledgement policy.
Requests, commands, field operations, and transmission-interval changes receive typed protocol responses.
Fast-packet framing and reassembly cover minimum, maximum, malformed, timeout, ownership, and multi-network isolation cases.
BAM transmit and receive enforce sizes, order, completion, and timeout.
RTS/CTS windows, acknowledgement, routing, and concurrent-session ambiguity are checked.
Malformed announcements, non-classical frames, bad checksums, and truncated streams are rejected without panic.
Application and automatic protocol traffic have bounded admission with explicit failure.
A new TCP epoch reclaims network citizenship before enumeration or scheduled traffic resumes.
Claim, heartbeat, fast-packet, ISO transport, and reconnect timing use bounded deterministic checks.
Conditional fields and signed widths are enforced by the shared codec.
Source identity, timestamps, direction, payload ownership, and slow-subscriber failure are preserved.
Gateway-owned sessions are separate from source-authoritative Clients; readiness is acknowledged per epoch and sends never mutate Tx lists implicitly.
Every compiled solicited BEM verb has independent local request/reply wire evidence with bounded, origin-aware correlation and typed partial results.
Remote BEM uses the exact variable-length PGN-126720 manufacturer envelope and binds correlation to both addresses and connection/claim epochs.
CAN ASCII mode 6 and gateway-owned N2K Type-A ASCII preserve documented timestamps, direction, identifiers, addresses, priorities, PGNs, and payload bounds.
EBL read/write and live wire tracing preserve time, direction, valid checksum-stripped BST records, exact invalid/unframed bytes, and Type-2 assembled messages.
